title: Initiative Entitlements Matrix and Cross-Org OKR Alignment Protocol
creator: Asha Menon
description:
Problem: We lack a single source of truth for how company-level OKRs map to owned initiatives, squad entitlements, and contingent resource credits. This causes repeated debates during quarterly planning, missed handoffs, and opaque escalation paths when priorities shift.

Goal: Deliver an Initiative Entitlements Matrix (IEM) and a lightweight alignment protocol that: 1) makes primary owners and entitled capacity explicit for each company-level OKR; 2) codifies how initiative credits shift when scope moves; 3) provides a minimal data schema and Console views for PMs/Eng leads to evaluate cross-team load during roadmap commits.

Scope:
- Define the IEM schema (OKR -> initiative -> squad ownership -> entitlements: FTE-days, infra credits, priority lanes).
- Establish decision rules and an escalation ladder for reassigning entitlements mid-cycle.
- Prototype two Console widgets: (a) Entitlement Heatmap; (b) Initiative Ripple Preview (simulates downstream impact when entitlement is reduced).
- Provide playbook steps for quarterly planning and ad-hoc emergent re-prioritization.

Out of scope: fully automating budgeting or replacing finance resource flows; detailed payroll or hiring plans.

Success metrics:
- Reduce cross-functional alignment meeting time by 30% during PI planning.
- >90% of initiatives have an assigned entitlement and owner before cycle kickoff.
- Console widgets adopted by #product and #eng leads for at least 3 teams in next cycle.
acceptance_criteria: IEM schema documented and approved by Product, Eng, and Finance reps
Escalation protocol published and tested in 1 tabletop exercise
Mock Console widgets implemented as read-only prototypes and linked in PRD
At least 10 company-level initiatives annotated with entitlements and owners
Rollout playbook with step-by-step facilitator checklist completed
